back: The time taken for a project's net cash inflows to recover the initial outlay.
Initial outlay ÷ annual net cash inflow.
Full years before recovery + (unrecovered outlay at start of the year ÷ inflow of that year). Multiply the fraction by 12 for months.

front: Average annual profit and average investment
back: Average profit = (total inflows - outlay) ÷ years. Average investment = initial outlay ÷ 2 (no residual value).
Accept if payback is within the maximum period; the shorter payback is preferred.
Accept if ARR is at least the target rate; the higher ARR is preferred.
Ignores cash flows after payback and the time value of money; the maximum period is arbitrary.
Uses profits not cash, ignores timing and the time value of money, and depends on depreciation policy.
